title: Style-veto bypass: tracer's combined-alert route never calls can_alert()
evidence: thresholds.can_alert() is called only from scanner.py (3 sites). tracer._crossref_findings_with_candidates() calls alert_combined_match() with no veto check. Live data/candidates/latest.json: 28 of 50 candidates carry style vetoes; 15 of them exceed tracer's 0.65 gate.
impact: A CRITICAL 'Fund Trace + Behavioral Match' email can be sent for a wallet the system has explicitly vetoed as behaviourally incompatible. This is the exact 'reach the inbox sideways' hole thresholds.can_alert() documents as closed, and README asserts as an invariant.
cause: Veto enforcement was added to scanner.py's routes but tracer.py has an independent, older copy of the same rule.
fix: tracer._crossref_findings_with_candidates now routes through thresholds.combined_alert_ok, which calls can_alert() first, so every alert route consults the style vetoes.
verification: tests/test_threshold_coherence.py::test_combined_alert_refuses_a_style_vetoed_candidate; measured on live candidates the route fires for 9 wallets instead of 29, the 20 suppressed being 15 style-vetoed and 5 score-decayed, all retained on the watchlist. Mutation-tested: re-introducing the bypass fails the suite.

title: Hardcoded 0.65 similarity gate in four decision modules bypasses thresholds.py
evidence: Only scanner.py and backtest.py call th.resolve(). Resolved operating thresholds are low=0.5963 medium=0.6463 high=0.6963 (ceiling 0.7163), so 0.65 corresponds to no tier boundary at all.
impact: A WATCH_CLOSELY candidate (0.6463-0.65) contributes zero corroboration to transfer-graph grading, zero continuity signal and zero risk points, while thresholds.py's docstring and README both assert it is the only place thresholds are decided.
cause: thresholds.py unification covered the scanner/alert/dashboard path but never the corroboration, grading and risk paths.
fix: thresholds.behavioural_gate() and behavioural_strength() added; risk.py, tracer.py and transfer_graph.py (3 sites) migrated off the 0.65 literal. continuity.HIGH_CONFIDENCE_MIN checked and deliberately left: it gates an aggregated continuity confidence, not a similarity score.
verification: tests/test_threshold_coherence.py (gate/strength/route tests). Mutation-tested: returning the old literal from behavioural_gate fails the suite.

title: Headline risk score structurally under-reports its strongest signal
evidence: top_candidate (weight 22) is scaled (score-0.65)/0.35, reaching full weight only at score 1.0. The proven self-match ceiling — what the real trader scores against his own history — is 0.7163. Measured: 0.6963 (CONFIRMED tier) -> 2.91/22 pts (13.2%); ceiling 0.7163 -> 4.17/22 (18.9%); 0.6463 (WATCH_CLOSELY) -> 0 pts.
impact: Even a perfect re-identification of the trader can contribute under 19% of the weight the design allocates to it. Live risk/latest.json reads 26.1 GUARDED while the target is 8.2 days silent, has abandoned his signature markets, and a confirmed-tier candidate exists.
cause: The [0.65, 1.0] band was written before the self-match ceiling was measured and never revisited.
fix: top_candidate is scaled between the resolved gate and the proven self-match ceiling instead of an unreachable 1.0.
verification: A CONFIRMED-tier candidate now earns a substantial majority of the 22 points rather than 2.91, and the ceiling earns all of them; on live data the posture reads 40.5 rather than 26.1. Mutation-tested.

title: Combined alert fires on all-time best score, latching on stale evidence
evidence: Uses c['best_score'] though the record also carries latest_score, recent_avg_score and last_seen. Live data: 18 of 29 gated candidates have best_score >= latest_score+0.10; worst 0xf28e1b06e00e best=0.7113 latest=0.1322.
impact: A wallet that currently scores 0.13 still produces a CRITICAL email asserting it 'matches the behavioral fingerprint', repeating every 12h (cooldown) for as long as it remains a fund-flow destination.
cause: best_score is the convenient field; freshness was never considered on this route.
fix: utils.candidate_current_score() is the single definition of how well a wallet matches now; adopted by tracer.py, risk.py, transfer_graph.py and, via api.currentScore(), the dashboard.
verification: tests/test_threshold_coherence.py::test_combined_alert_refuses_a_candidate_whose_score_has_decayed. Mutation-tested: reverting to best_score fails the suite.

title: The same 'fund-flow destination + behavioural match' rule is implemented twice, divergently
evidence: Both implement 'deposited_to_hl AND behaviourally matches -> alert_combined_match'. scanner uses eff['medium'] + can_alert() + current score; tracer uses hardcoded 0.65 + no veto check + all-time best_score.
impact: Two systems control the same outcome with different answers — the precise failure mode thresholds.py was created to end.
cause: tracer's copy predates the thresholds unification and was not migrated.
fix: scanner._combined_route() selects the route and thresholds.combined_alert_ok() applies its bar plus the veto check; scanner.py and tracer.py now share both.
verification: tests/test_threshold_coherence.py::test_scanner_route_selection_keeps_its_documented_precedence and ::test_combined_alert_route_thresholds_match_the_scanner_branches. The second independent audit diffed the refactor against 23b28d852 and confirmed identical precedence and per-route thresholds.

title: README states the wrong test count
evidence: README says 'expect: 156 passed'; measured suite is 340 passed.
impact: A developer following the setup checklist cannot tell a healthy suite from a broken one.
cause: Count not updated as tests were added.
verification: Suite is 375 at the certified commit; README updated and kept in step.

title: docs/architecture.md describes components that were never built
evidence: Self-flagged in README 'Known rough edges': describes Svelte components, stores.js and utils.js that do not exist, plus ~10x optimistic storage estimates.
impact: Actively misleads future work; a reader who trusts it builds against a fictional design.
fix: Deliberately not fixed. docs/architecture.md already carries a staleness banner naming exactly the components that were never built, and rewriting it is outside the frozen V1 boundary.
verification: Banner verified present at the top of the document; README also flags it under Known rough edges. Recorded as carried rather than fixed so the summary sentence in CHECKPOINT.md stays literally true.

title: Untracked local backup directories are not gitignored in a public repo
evidence: git status shows three untracked backup trees; .gitignore does not cover them.
impact: A single 'git add -A' would publish full repository snapshots to a public repository. Also keeps the working tree permanently dirty, which blocks clean release validation.
cause: Backups were taken into the working tree rather than outside it.
fix: Ezekiel-backup-*/ added to .gitignore so a stray `git add -A` cannot publish a full snapshot to what must remain a public repository.
verification: git check-ignore confirms all three backup directories match; the third independent audit re-verified this against .gitignore:18. The directories themselves were never touched.

title: Dead CSS selector emitted as a build warning
evidence: vite-plugin-svelte: 'Unused CSS selector .result-wallet a' on every build.
impact: Dead styling left behind by the Hypurrscan link change (9716b863e); warns on every CI build so real warnings are easier to miss.
fix: The selector targeted an anchor that had moved inside <Addr>, where scoped CSS cannot reach it; replaced with a :global() rule so scanner addresses regain the monospace styling every other address on the site has.
verification: Production build emits no warnings; the scanner route was rendered in headless Chrome and inspected.

title: Decision-frequency veto measures presence, not style, and rejected the target as an impostor against his own history
evidence: LIVE profile/backtest.json 2026-08-05T01:43 on origin/main: passed=false, self_score 0.45, self_rank 8, margin -0.1185, failures include "self-match tripped style vetoes: ['Decision frequency 6x apart (0.17 vs 0.94 position episodes/day)']". Both windows held 12 active trading days; they differed only in calendar spread (19 vs 72 days). episodes_per_day divided by calendar span, so intermittency read as a different human. Recomputed from the live report's own figures: per active day the ratio is 1.5x, not 5.5x, and the activity similarity components rise 0.4253->0.8278 and 0.4591->0.8937.
impact: The self-match failure put the live scanner into OBSERVING with raw config thresholds 0.90/0.80/0.65 and behavioural alerting DISABLED (confirmed in live data/scans/latest.json 2026-08-05T07:46). The product's primary detection vector for its primary journey was offline in production. active_days_ratio already measured presence, so intermittency was being counted three times, once as a hard veto.
cause: Window selection was fixed to use distinct active days rather than a calendar period; the metric the veto reads was left calendar-normalised, so the same conflation reappeared one layer down.
fix: episodes_per_active_day / fills_per_active_day; active_days_ratio clamped to <=1 and left as the single measure of presence; keys renamed so a pre-change fingerprint drops the dimension rather than comparing mismatched units; SCORING_SCHEMA bumped to 2026-08-05.1 so the old ceiling cannot carry forward.
verification: Local end-to-end rebuild+backtest: PASS, self-match 0.7461 (was 0.7163), rank 1 of 21, margin 0.1434, self_vetoes [], failures [], activity dimension 0.834 (production reported 0.4583).

title: Dashboard tiers and labels the all-time best score, disagreeing with the backend that grades on the current one
evidence: getAlertState read candidates[0].best_score, and candidates/latest.json is persisted sorted by best_score, so the banner named the all-time leader at its peak. Verified against LIVE production data 2026-08-05: candidates[0] is 0xcbd909 with best_score 0.7505 but latest_score 0.45, while the wallet that actually matches best now is 0x12e16e at 0.7019.
impact: README promises the displayed tier and the emailed tier always agree. The banner asserted a 75% behavioural match for a wallet currently at 45%, and the transfers page showed a behavioural score the backend had not used for the classification displayed beside it.
cause: Same root cause as F-004 on the JavaScript side; no shared definition of 'current score' across the language boundary.
fix: api.currentScore() mirrors utils.candidate_current_score(); api.topCandidate() re-ranks instead of trusting file order.

title: Dashboard alert banner latches on fund-flow signals the backend has already expired
evidence: getAlertState used findings.some(f => f.deposited_to_hl) and filtered HL counterparties on total_out_usd alone, both unbounded in time, while risk._gather_signals bounds the same signals to RECENT_SIGNAL_DAYS=21. Confirmed against live production data 2026-08-05: the only two deposited_to_hl findings were detected 2026-07-03, 33.3 days old; the backend reported l1_outbound=false while the dashboard banner showed level=critical. fund_flows/latest.json keeps its last 100 findings with no expiry, so the latch is permanent.
impact: The operator's top-level banner had been showing a red CRITICAL about a month-old fund movement every day for a month, while the backend's own risk score had correctly expired it. A banner that is always red is not a signal, and this product's whole value rests on the operator still trusting an alert when it matters. The local variable was even named freshOut with nothing checking freshness.
cause: Signal expiry was added to risk.py (RECENT_SIGNAL_DAYS) but never mirrored on the dashboard, which computes its banner independently from the same files.
fix: api.isRecentSignal()/RECENT_SIGNAL_DAYS mirror risk.py, applied to both the fund-flow and HL-native branches; an undated finding is treated as ancient, matching risk._detected_ts. risk.py:191 also now uses its own constant instead of a repeated literal 21.
verification: Against live data the banner changes from level=critical (stale) to level=watch 'Watchlisted behavioral lead at 70.2%', agreeing with the backend; isRecentSignal(null/undefined/garbage/0) all false.

title: account/latest.json was never published, so the drawdown signal and the liquidation alert were both silently dead
where: src/collector.py collect_positions (no save_latest for account/); src/risk.py _gather_signals; src/collector.py check_account_value_drop
evidence: collect_positions snapshots {perp,spot,hip3} into the dated account/ directory but never called save_latest, so data/account/latest.json still held a portfolio payload left by an older collector - a LIST. Both readers do data.get('perp', data), which raises AttributeError on a list, and both swallowed it (except Exception: pass / return). Live 2026-08-05: account/latest.json is a list of 8; live risk/latest.json shows drawdown_pct 0.0; and data/state/ contains no account_high_water_cents.txt or prev_account_value_cents.txt at all, because the cursor that risk.py needs is written INSIDE the function that was bailing out.
impact: Two features dead for as long as that file has been stale: the drawdown signal, forfeiting 12 of the 100 risk points, and alert_account_value_drop ('Possible Liquidation'), which never fired once. A trader who has been wiped starting again on a fresh wallet is one of the migration precursors this system exists to catch. The whole chain was broken, not one link.
cause: save_latest was added for positions, spot and each HIP-3 dex but never for the composite account state; the resulting stale file then failed shape checks that were swallowed by bare excepts.
fix: collect_positions now publishes the composite via save_latest. Both readers reject a non-dict payload explicitly and print a warning, so a drawdown of 0.0 can only mean 'measured, no drawdown', never 'could not read the file'.
verification: tests/test_account_latest_freshness.py - 6 tests covering publication, shape, snapshot parity, drawdown computation, high-water cursor establishment, and that an unreadable state is announced rather than swallowed.

title: Two contradictory 'Account Value' figures on the same screen
where: dashboard/src/routes/+page.svelte stat tile and chart heading
evidence: The tile summed perp + HIP-3 margin accounts; the chart plotted Hyperliquid's portfolio series, which also includes spot. Measured live 2026-08-05: $6.07M perp + $5.60M HIP-3 = $11.67M on the tile, against $34.51M on the chart, the gap being $28.6M of spot USDC. Both were labelled 'Account Value'.
impact: The operator's first screen showed one quantity appearing to contradict itself by roughly 3x. Both numbers were accurate to their own source; neither label said which source.
cause: The tile and the chart were built from different endpoints and given the same name.
fix: Tile relabelled 'Margin Account Value'; chart heading 'Portfolio Value' with an 'incl. spot' qualifier. No computation changed - this was a labelling defect, and the arithmetic was verified before renaming rather than guessed.
verification: Rendered in headless Chrome against the production build and live data; both labels confirmed present and distinct.
